title: From screen appearance to rates on screen
prompt: Put the steps of Pocket Budget's exchange-rate screen in the order they happen at runtime, from the moment the screen appears to the moment the rates are visible.
hints: Nothing happens until SwiftUI starts the async work, and the user should see a spinner before any network call begins.
You can't fetch before you have a URL, and you shouldn't decode before you know the response is a success.
The last step is the one that makes SwiftUI redraw.
explanation:
`.task` starts `model.load()` when the view appears. The model sets `.loading` first so the spinner shows immediately. The client builds the URL with its query items, then `URLSession.shared.data(from:)` suspends until the response arrives. The status check comes before decoding, because URLSession doesn't throw for a 404 or 500 and an error page would fail to decode with a misleading message. Decoding produces a `RatesResponse`, and assigning `.loaded(response)` on the main actor is what makes SwiftUI re-render the list.

If any step after `set-loading` throws, the model's single `catch` sets `.failed(message)` instead.

items.start-task: SwiftUI runs `.task { await model.load() }` as the view appears
items.set-loading: The model sets `state = .loading`, so the view shows a `ProgressView`
items.decode: `try decoder.decode(RatesResponse.self, from: data)` with snake_case and ISO 8601 strategies
items.set-loaded: Assign `state = .loaded(response)` on the main actor, and SwiftUI redraws the list
